script.spoken: What If Ice Sank Instead of Floating? Most substances shrink as they freeze. Water doesn't. Ice is about 8.3% less dense than liquid water. Liquid water is densest at 4 °C. If ice sank, lakes would freeze from the bottom up. Each winter's ice would pile up, shielded from summer sun. Floating ice instead insulates the water beneath it. So a strange quirk of water keeps lakes alive in winter.

Some glaciers are spitting out icebergs and draining the Greenland ice sheet at an alarming pace; others are barely moving; a few are growing thicker.
